scenes.title: COUNT
scenes.narration: COUNT tallies how many rows or values exist, the first aggregate function most people learn.

scenes.title: Counting rows
scenes.narration: COUNT star counts every row in the group, regardless of its contents. Passing a column name instead counts only rows where that column is not NULL. It is frequently paired with GROUP BY to count rows within each category.

scenes.title: Counting per group
scenes.narration: GROUP BY collapses the employees into one row per department. COUNT star then tallies how many employees fall in each group. The alias headcount gives the resulting number a clear, readable name.

scenes.heading: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col)
scenes.narration: COUNT star measures the total number of rows in each group, NULLs included. COUNT of a specific column instead ignores rows where that column is NULL. Choosing between them depends on whether you want total rows or only rows with a value present.

scenes.text: COUNT answers how many, but be deliberate about whether NULLs should count.
scenes.narration: Use COUNT to tally rows, and decide up front whether COUNT star or COUNT of a column fits, since only the latter skips NULLs.
